title: Where do seven composite numbers come one after another below 100?
description: A long gap between two neighbouring primes is found in the list, and the numbers lying inside it are tested one by one. All of them turn out composite.
teaching_notes: One idea: all the numbers between two neighbouring primes are composite, so a long gap between primes gives a long run of composite numbers. Watch for students who test random numbers instead of using the gaps in the list.

video_script.why: The child looks for a long gap in the list of primes, because everything inside a gap is crossed out and so composite.
video_script.substitution: Find two neighbouring primes that are eight apart and test the seven numbers between them.
video_script.anchor: The list of primes up to 100 with a stretch of crossed out numbers between two neighbouring primes
video_script.payoff_line: The numbers from ninety to ninety six are seven consecutive composite numbers.

final_answer.spoken: seven composite numbers lie in a row

maths_rules: primes 89 and 97 are neighbours and 97 - 89 = 8, so 7 numbers lie between them: 90, 91, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96
each has a factor other than 1 and itself, so each is composite
video_script.design: Two neighbouring primes are drawn as teal posts with the seven numbers between them as amber cards.

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Step one, look for a long gap in the list. Eighty nine and ninety seven are neighbouring primes, and ninety seven take away eighty nine is eight.

narration: <bookmark mark='even'/>Step two, test each of the seven numbers. Ninety, ninety two, ninety four and ninety six are even, so two divides them.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>Ninety one is seven times thirteen. Ninety three is three times thirty one, and ninety five is five times nineteen.

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step three, check the run. There are seven numbers, and none of them is in the list of primes.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The numbers from ninety to ninety six are seven consecutive composite numbers.
